gaps.sentence: I'd love ___ help with the decorating, if you're free.
gaps.explanation: 'Some' is used in requests and hopes where the speaker wants agreement.
'Neither of my parents is ...' is correct for two items with a singular verb; 'both/all' need a plural verb and 'none' is not used for two.

gaps.sentence: He was driving ___ fast for the icy road.
gaps.explanation: 'Too fast for something' means faster than is safe; 'so fast' needs a 'that' clause, not 'for'.

gaps.sentence: Some metals are magnetic; ___ are not.
gaps.explanation: 'Some ... others ...' contrasts unspecified groups; 'the others' would need a closed, known set.

gaps.hint: general statement without 'the' — 'people' has no article
gaps.explanation: 'Most people' means people in general; 'most of' needs 'the' (most of the people).

gaps.sentence: We had very ___ rain this spring, so the garden suffered.
gaps.explanation: 'Little' means not much and is used with uncountables; the garden suffering shows an insufficient amount.

gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.

gaps.sentence: He had ___ money, so he couldn't even buy a bus ticket.
gaps.explanation: 'Had no money' states zero and explains the result; 'none' cannot stand directly before a noun.
